pr.title: [beta] Revert "Replace NullOp::SizeOf and NullOp::AlignOf by lang items."
pr.description:
Totally clean revert, tests pass on my local machine.

Fixes rust-lang/rust#149081 on 1.92 beta

cc @lcnr @BoxyUwU @jieyouxu @cjgillot
pr.author: wesleywiser

issues.title: 1.92 regression in PyO3: unable to determine layout for ... because ... cannot be normalized
issues.body:
```
[INFO] [stdout] error[E0080]: unable to determine layout for `<<T as PyClassImpl>::BaseType as PyClassBaseType>::LayoutAsBase` because `<<T as PyClassImpl>::BaseType as PyClassBaseType>::LayoutAsBase` cannot be normalized
[INFO] [stdout]  --> /rustc/f3f12444a017add0468f683f3a10656d29438a05/library/core/src/mem/mod.rs:1247:26
[INFO] [stdout]   |
[INFO] [stdout]   = note: evaluation of `<pycell::impl_::PyClassObject<T> as std::mem::SizedTypeProperties>::ALIGN` failed here
[INFO] [stdout] 
[INFO] [stdout]

```

* https://crater-reports.s3.amazonaws.com/beta-1.92-4/beta-2025-11-10/gh/umar052001.blitzparse/log.txt
* https://crater-reports.s3.amazonaws.com/beta-1.92-4/beta-2025-11-10/gh/Jayson-Fong.python-libbruteforce/log.txt

processing.reason: The PR's incorrect transformation is purely a compiler-internal change in how MIR represents a layout query: `Rvalue::NullaryOp(NullOp::SizeOf|AlignOf, ty)` versus evaluating the lang-item associated constants `<T as SizedTypeProperties>::SIZE|ALIGN`. For every concrete, sized type that successfully compiles, both forms yield the same `layout.size`/`layout.align` bytes, so ordinary source functions using either representation agree at runtime. The regression is compile-time, not a wrong runtime value: the associated-const form adds an extra const-eval/layout query and therefore turns normalization-sensitive or cyclic layouts into diagnostics such as `unable to determine layout ... cannot be normalized` or `a cycle occurred during layout computation`. The changed regression material confirms this: the relevant tests are build-fail/UI tests (`layout-cycle`, `const-size-of-cycle`, `issue-80742`, etc.), Miri fail tests, and MIR-dump expectations, not run-pass value tests. Reproducing the failure would require a transformed function that fails to compile, which cannot also pass Miri; using an ordinary type makes both variants return identical values. Unsized inputs are explicitly invalid/precondition-violating for these nullary ops and the associated-const form is also `Sized`-bounded. Thus no source-grounded pair can be validated that both passes Miri on the same inputs and produces different defined values without manufacturing an unrelated semantic change.

analysis.summary: A 1.92 beta regression was caused by replacing MIR `NullOp::SizeOf`/`NullOp::AlignOf` with lang-item associated constants (`SizedTypeProperties::SIZE`/`ALIGN`). Evaluating those associated constants introduced an extra const-evaluation/layout query and failed when the type layout required normalization or formed a cycle. The PR reverts to nullary MIR operands and restores direct layout-based evaluation across lowering, const-prop, GVN, check insertion, promotion, validation, and simplification. No compiler was built or run; this is derived from the patch and test-expectation changes.
analysis.originalLogic: Originally, `size_of`/`align_of` intrinsics are lowered to `Rvalue::NullaryOp(NullOp::SizeOf | NullOp::AlignOf, ty)`. These nullary ops have type `usize` and are evaluated directly from the type layout in const-eval, const-prop, GVN, and codegen. `CheckNull`, `CheckAlignment`, and `InstSimplify` synthesize the same nullary ops when they need size/alignment. Promotion/validation treat them as normal promotable and valid rvalues.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect transformation replaced the nullary MIR ops with lang-item associated constants: `Operand::unevaluated_constant(tcx, LangItem::SizeOf/AlignOf, &[ty.into()], span)`, i.e. `<T as SizedTypeProperties>::SIZE` / `ALIGN`. It also removed the `NullOp::SizeOf`/`AlignOf` arms from MIR consumers. This changed direct layout queries into const-evaluation of an associated constant, which introduced an extra const/layout query and broke cases needing normalization or cycles. The correction restores `Rvalue::NullaryOp(NullOp::SizeOf/AlignOf, ty)` and guards unsized layouts where folding is invalid.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust MIR/codegen inputs involving `core::mem::size_of`/`align_of`, box allocation lowering, `align_of_val` on slices, null/alignment checks, and const-generic/associated-type layout queries. Especially types whose layout requires normalization or forms a cycle, e.g. the reported `<<T as PyClassImpl>::BaseType as PyClassBaseType>::LayoutAsBase`, and test types such as `Inline<T> where [u8; size_of::<T>() + 1]:` / `A<dyn Trait>`.
analysis.trigger: A `size_of`/`align_of` operation is evaluated in a context where the type layout is not immediately available and requires normalization, or participates in a layout cycle. Under the lang-item transformation this becomes const-evaluation of `<T as SizedTypeProperties>::SIZE/ALIGN`, producing an extra const query and an error such as `unable to determine layout ... because ... cannot be normalized` or `a cycle occurred during layout computation`. The same transformation also affects synthesized checks and slice `align_of_val` simplification.
preconditions: A program uses `size_of`/`align_of` directly, through box allocation lowering, through `align_of_val` on a slice, or through inserted null/alignment checks.
The queried type layout must be computed during const-eval or MIR optimization; normalization-sensitive or cyclic layouts expose the regression.
For safe constant folding of `SizeOf`/`AlignOf`, the type must be sized; unsized layouts are not valid inputs to these nullary ops.
The transformation under test must swap only the representation of the size/alignment operation, not unrelated control flow or operand order.
pitfalls: `NullOp::SizeOf`/`AlignOf` are not meaningful for unsized types. The interpreter uses `span_bug!` for unsized `NullaryOp::SizeOf`/`AlignOf`, and codegen asserts `type_is_sized`; MIR constructors/validation must preserve the `Sized` requirement.

Const-prop and GVN must not fold an unsized layout. `DataflowConstProp` only matches `NullOp::SizeOf if layout.is_sized()` / `NullOp::AlignOf if layout.is_sized()`, and GVN explicitly returns `None` when the layout is unsized.

Replacing the nullary op with an unevaluated associated-const operand is not semantics-preserving: it adds a const-evaluation query and can turn a layout failure into an associated-const evaluation failure.

The revert restores known bugs for some `generic_const_exprs` unsized cases; those tests were moved back to `known-bug`/`crashes`, so the revert is not a general correctness fix for unsized `size_of`.
Do not conflate promotion legality with implementation validity: `PromoteTemps` permits `NullOp::SizeOf`/`AlignOf`, while `Validator`/borrowck type checking still enforces the `Sized` bound.
`align_of_val` simplification on a slice must produce `AlignOf(elem_ty)`, not an unevaluated `<elem_ty as SizedTypeProperties>::ALIGN` constant.
analysis.testStrategy: Use MIR-opt tests that emit before/after MIR for `LowerIntrinsics` on generic `size_of`/`align_of` functions: the after-MIR must contain `_0 = SizeOf(T)` / `_0 = AlignOf(T)` and `goto`, not an intrinsic call or `<T as SizedTypeProperties>::...` const. Add GVN const-prop tests (e.g. box expressions) showing `SizeOf(i32)`/`AlignOf(i32)` folded to `const 4_usize` where appropriate, and tests ensuring unsized cases are not folded. Check `InstSimplify` on `align_of_val(slice)` emits `AlignOf(T)`, and check box/null/alignment MIR no longer mentions `SizedTypeProperties::SIZE/ALIGN`. Include UI/compile-fail tests for cyclic/normalization-sensitive layouts and unsized generic-const cases, comparing diagnostics for the nullary-op versus lang-item representation. Verify promotion/validation accepts `NullOp::SizeOf`/`AlignOf` only with a sized type.
